source.title_on_document: Groups and AI: How Access to Generative AI Influences Creative Teamwork

supplement.where: The paper refers only to Appendix A (user creations) and Appendix B (Figure 4, Study 1 questionnaire ratings), both inside this PDF (pp. 415-421). No online supplement is mentioned.
supplement.holds: Nothing outside this PDF. No table of means, SDs, or standard errors exists anywhere; rating levels appear only as bar charts (Figure 2, Figure 4).

paper_design_summary: Study 1: six co-located groups of three (18 people, university convenience sample) each did two 20-minute marketing-campaign ideation tasks (product name, slogan, 2-3 selling points, sketch), one with ChatGPT-4o and one with Google search only; condition and product order were counterbalanced. Participants self-rated their group's result and process; sessions were video-coded. Study 2: 20 external online raters, blind to AI use, rated and ranked the 12 campaign results from Study 1 on six Creative Product Semantic Scale items.

studies.label: Study 1 (lab, groups of three, ChatGPT vs Google search, within-group) with outcomes scored by Study 2 external raters

assignment.what_was_assigned: Order of the two conditions (AI = ChatGPT-4o vs No AI = Google search without AI) and the pairing of condition with product (Glowing Umbrella vs Smart Plant Pot); every group did both conditions. The paper says counterbalanced, not randomized.
assignment.quote: The order of conditions and products was counterbalanced across 6 trials, ensuring that each combination was used once.

arms.name: AI
arms.description: Group had ChatGPT-4o on a shared 55-inch screen during the ~20-minute task.

arms.name: No AI
arms.description: Group had the Google search engine without AI functionality, no AI tools, during the ~20-minute task.

participants.exclusions: None reported. 18 people in 6 groups of three; every person took part in both conditions (within-group design), so each arm contains the same 18 people / 6 groups.
participants.who: University convenience sample, aged 20 to 29 (mean 25.6), 9 male and 9 female, mostly computer science/STEM background, all prior AI-tool users; not compensated. The paper says 'university context' and 'professional background' and does not state that all were students.
participants.country: not_stated (authors at RWTH Aachen University, Germany; study run in English)
participants.quote: 18 people (9 male, 9 female) aged 20 to 29 years (mean = 25.6, SD = 2.7) participated in Study 1.
participants.locator: p. 409, Section 3.1; p. 412, Section 8 ('six groups of three')

ai_tool.how_used: Free use of ChatGPT on a shared screen by the whole group; groups prompted it for names and slogans and most generated at least five images per session to guide the hand sketch (p. 410, Section 4.2.1; p. 412, Section 4.2.3).

task.description: Ideate a marketing campaign for a fictitious product (Glow-in-the-dark Umbrella or Smart Plant Pot): name the product, write a slogan, list 2-3 core selling points, and sketch the product and a logo with pen and paper, on a structured worksheet.

outcomes.name: External rating: Conventional/Original (Creative Product Semantic Scale item)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: 20 external online raters, blind to AI use, rated all 6 results per campaign on a -2 to 2 bipolar scale; analyzed with Aligned Rank Transform nonparametric ANOVA (Use of AI x Campaign) with Holm-corrected Wilcoxon post-hoc tests. Raters mostly technical background, 3 with creative background.

contrasts.reported: No significant effect reported for this item; means and SD whiskers shown only as bars in Figure 2 (Study 2 panel), no numbers printed.

outcomes.name: External rating: Predictable/Unexpected (Creative Product Semantic Scale item)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Same 20 external raters, -2 to 2 scale, ART ANOVA.

contrasts.reported: No significant effect reported; bars only in Figure 2 (Study 2 panel).

outcomes.name: External rating: Disorganized/Organized (Creative Product Semantic Scale item)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Same 20 external raters, -2 to 2 scale, ART ANOVA; organization of the campaign result.

contrasts.reported: Effect of Use of AI F1,57=5.43, p <= 0.05; interaction Campaign x Use of AI F1,57=20.45, p <= 0.001; post-hoc: Smart Plant Pot x AI significantly more organized than Smart Plant Pot x No AI and Glowing Umbrella x AI (p <= 0.05).

outcomes.name: External rating: Impractical/Practical (Creative Product Semantic Scale item)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Same 20 external raters, -2 to 2 scale, ART ANOVA.

contrasts.reported: Interaction Use of AI x Campaign on Practicability F1,57=4.8, p <= 0.05; no main effect reported. 'The post-hoc test only showed higher ratings for the Smart Plant Pot for AI in comparison to No AI (p <= 0.05).'

outcomes.name: External rating: Unappealing/Appealing (Creative Product Semantic Scale item)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Same 20 external raters, -2 to 2 scale, ART ANOVA; appeal of the campaign result.

contrasts.reported: Interaction Use of AI x Campaign on Appeal F1,57=10.12, p <= 0.01; no main effect reported. Post-hoc: higher ratings for the Smart Plant Pot for AI vs No AI (p <= 0.05).

outcomes.name: External rating: Unfocused/Well-defined ('focus', Creative Product Semantic Scale item)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Same 20 external raters, -2 to 2 scale, ART ANOVA; how focused/well-defined the result is.

contrasts.reported: Effect of Use of AI F1,57=4.38, p <= 0.05; interaction Use of AI x Campaign F1,57=7.47, p <= 0.01; 'AI results were perceived as significantly more well-defined'; post-hoc: Smart Plant Pot x AI significantly more focused than Glowing Umbrella x AI and Smart Plant Pot x No AI (p <= 0.05).

outcomes.name: External preference ranking of results (rank 1 to 6 within campaign)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Each of the 20 external raters ranked the 6 results per campaign by preference; Figure 3 shows the frequency of each rank for AI and No AI results (axis to 120 rankings per condition). No test reported.

contrasts.reported: 'AI results were ranked slightly better.' (Figure 3 caption); no numbers or test printed.

outcomes.name: Self-ratings of own group's result on the same six Creative Product Semantic Scale items (Study 1 participants)
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: Participants rated their own group's result on originality, organization, practicability, predictability, appeal, definition (-2 to 2); Wilcoxon signed-rank tests. Recorded for completeness; self-ratings by the creators do not meet criterion 3.

contrasts.reported: Only cognitive effort differed significantly (Z = -3.18, p <= 0.01); 'No other significant effects were found'. Item means shown only as bars in Figure 2 (Study 1 panel).

studies.label: Study 2 (online external rating of Study 1 results)

assignment.what_was_assigned: Nothing was assigned to raters. Only the order of campaigns and of the Study 1 results shown was randomized.
assignment.quote: The orders of Campaigns and the results from Study 1 were randomized.

participants.who: External raters aged 18 to 53 (mean 27.55), 7 male and 13 female; 13 with a technical background (e.g., computer science, medicine), 3 with a creative background (architecture, design). Blind to whether AI was used.
participants.quote: 20 people (7 male, 13 female) aged 18 to 53 years (mean = 27.55, SD = 8.09) participated in Study 2.

ai_tool.how_used: No AI use by raters; they rated outputs produced in Study 1.

task.description: Rate all 12 Study 1 campaign results on six Creative Product Semantic Scale items, then rank the 6 results within each campaign by preference.

company_involvement.description: No company involvement stated. Funded in part by the German B-IT Foundation.

eligibility.reason: Within-group lab experiment with only 18 people (6 groups of three), far below 50. AI access was experimenter-manipulated within each group, but the order of conditions and products was counterbalanced, not stated as randomized (criterion 1 unclear). External blind ratings of the group outputs meet criterion 3. Belongs in the screening report as an experiment under 50 participants.

one_line_finding: With 6 groups of three (18 people), 20 blind external raters judged ChatGPT-assisted marketing campaigns significantly more organized (F1,57=5.43, p <= 0.05) and well-defined (F1,57=4.38, p <= 0.05) than web-search campaigns, with no reported difference in originality or unexpectedness, and ranked AI results slightly better (p. 410, Section 4.1; p. 411, Figures 2-3).
open_questions: The text says order was 'counterbalanced across 6 trials, ensuring that each combination was used once', but Appendix A shows the Glowing Umbrella done with AI by 2 groups (01, 04) and without AI by 4 groups (02, 03, 05, 06), and the Smart Plant Pot with AI by 4 groups and without by 2. Condition-by-product pairing is therefore unbalanced; the order of conditions per group is not reported.
The unit of the Study 2 ART ANOVA is not stated. The residual df of 57 is consistent with 20 raters x 4 Campaign x AI cells, but the paper does not say so.
notes: Study 2 has no assignment of AI; its ratings are the outcome measure for Study 1 outputs, so its outcomes are recorded under S1 (S1-O1 to S1-O7) and S2 has none. The 20 raters are not counted as experimental participants. Outputs are group-level: 12 campaign results in total (6 groups x 2 conditions). Other Study 1 measures not scored on the output and not listed as outcomes: NASA-TLX cognitive effort (AI mean = -0.56, SD = 0.78 vs No AI mean = 0.33, SD = 0.84; Z = -3.18, p <= 0.01; p. 410), team-effectiveness items, perceived creativity and enjoyment (Figure 4, Appendix B, p. 421), preference between conditions (7 AI, 4 No AI, 7 no preference), perceived AI role, and video-coded collaboration behaviors from reflexive thematic analysis (pp. 410-412). No means, SDs, or standard errors are printed for any output rating; only test statistics with p thresholds and bar charts.
